Feature Dependency Matrix
Resource sharing conflicts:
Unified Auth + Analytics API share the primary DB pool (cannot exceed 850 connections combined during any rollout phase)
Analytics API + Webhook Consolidation share compute cluster (cannot exceed 5,500 vCPU-hours combined during rollout)
All three features share CDN infrastructure (320 slot hard cap)
Engineering Operations Hard Limits
Monitoring Capacity
The SRE team can monitor a maximum of 4 concurrent rollout waves across all features. Each distinct customer segment (tier/region/percentage bracket) in an active rollout counts as one wave.
Customer Tier SLA Separation Rules
Enterprise tier customers CANNOT be in the same rollout wave as Starter tier customers (SLA guarantee conflict)
Professional tier can be grouped with either Enterprise OR Starter, but mixing all three tiers in one wave is prohibited
Mid-market accounts (subset of Professional tier) require dedicated monitoring and cannot share waves with Starter tier
Rollout Configuration Limits

Engineering can support up to 3 different rollout strategies running in parallel (e.g., one feature rolling by tier, another by region, another by percentage). Exceeding this creates unmanageable operational complexity.
Rollback Capability
Fast rollback (< 15 minutes) is only guaranteed for waves affecting fewer than 150 customers. Waves with 150+ customers require 45-90 minute rollback windows.

title: Platform API Migration - Legacy Auth Endpoint Deprecation Plan

blocks.text: API Migration Workflow - Dependency Chain
Critical path for legacy /v1/auth endpoint deprecation. Must complete before Q2 customer renewals.
Phase 1: Internal Service Migration (BLOCKING)
Status: 60% complete as of 2026-04-02
Remaining services: analytics-worker, reporting-batch, legacy-webhook-proxy
Engineering estimate: 5 days ±3 days (range: Apr 7-12)
Blocker: analytics-worker has hard-coded endpoint reference in 14 modules, refactor underway
Owner: Priya Sharma (platform-backend)
Phase 2: Customer Communication Preparation (PARALLEL RISK)
Draft customer notification email + migration guide
Legal review required (2-3 day turnaround)
DECISION POINT: Draft now (risk: date revisions if Phase 1 slips) vs. wait for Phase 1 completion (risk: insufficient notice period)
Rework cost if dates change: ~4 hours (re-draft + legal re-review)
Owner: Jorge Alvarez + Sarah Kim (Customer Success)
Phase 3: Customer Notification & Grace Period
Contractual SLA: 21-day notice minimum for API changes
Target customer migration window: 30 days (buffer for support load)
Uncertainty: customer response time unpredictable (historical range: 3-28 days)
Mid-market accounts (CUS-102, CUS-103, CUS-104) already showing churn signals - extra care needed
Phase 4: Kill-Switch Date
Proposed: May 15, 2026 (assumes Phase 1 complete by Apr 10, notification sent Apr 11, 30-day grace)
CRITICAL: If Phase 1 slips 1 week → kill-switch must move to May 22 to maintain 30-day grace
Fallback: Can compress grace to 21 days (contractual minimum) if absolutely necessary
Go/No-Go Checkpoint Structure
Checkpoint 1 (Apr 10): Internal migration health check
Criteria: All 3 services passing integration tests, no P0/P1 bugs, engineering sign-off via Workmail
GO → send customer notification Apr 11 | NO-GO → escalate to VP Engineering, revise timeline
Checkpoint 2 (Apr 25): Customer migration progress review
Criteria: >70% of API calls migrated to /v2/auth, <5 support escalations
GO → proceed to kill-switch May 15 | NO-GO → extend grace period, delay kill-switch
Parallel vs Serial Decision Rationale
PARALLEL (low rework cost): Draft migration guide content, prepare support KB articles, schedule CS team training
SERIAL (irreversible commitment): Customer notification email (contains specific dates), public changelog announcement, contractual notice
STRATEGY: Begin parallel work now (Apr 5), hold serial commitments until Checkpoint 1 passes

title: SRE Capacity Constraints & Rollback Buffer Policy - Polaris v1

blocks.text: SRE Capacity Constraints - April 2026
This document defines SRE capacity constraints and rollback buffer requirements for Polaris v1 GA launch windows in April 2026.
1. On-Call Rotation Schedule
Week of April 14: Marcus Chen (primary), David Torres (secondary) - 12 SRE hours available
Week of April 21: Sarah Kim (primary - auth focus), Marcus Chen (secondary) - 16 SRE hours available, split coverage
Week of April 28: Marcus Chen (primary), Rachel Kim (secondary) - 20 SRE hours available, full coverage
2. Infrastructure Allocation by Window
Window A (Apr 14-15): 85% compute, 70% database pool, 80% CDN capacity
Window B (Apr 21-22): 90% compute, 80% database pool, 85% CDN capacity
Window C (Apr 28-29): 95% compute, 90% database pool, 95% CDN capacity
3. Rollback Buffer Policy
3.1 Policy Statement

All platform launches require a minimum 72-hour rollback readiness buffer before the next critical platform milestone or hard-gated event (e.g., auth migration checkpoints, leadership reviews, customer-facing feature releases).
3.2 Rationale

72-hour buffer ensures: (1) adequate time for rollback execution if launch issues are detected; (2) post-rollback validation and system stabilization; (3) incident retrospective and communication to stakeholders; (4) no resource contention with subsequent platform events.
3.3 Constraint Violations
Window A: Rollback buffer ends April 17 EOD. Q2 Leadership Review on April 15 creates PM availability conflict during critical launch window. Not a buffer violation but an availability constraint.

Window B: Rollback buffer ends April 24 EOD. Auth Migration Checkpoint 2 on April 23 = only 48-hour buffer. VIOLATES 72-hour policy. Additionally, SRE coverage split between Polaris and auth creates resource contention risk.
Window C: Rollback buffer ends May 1 EOD. Next platform milestone (monitoring review) on May 2 = 96-hour buffer. SATISFIES 72-hour policy with 24-hour margin.
4. Recommended Window
Window C (April 28-29) is the only window that satisfies all hard constraints: adequate SRE capacity, no calendar conflicts, 72+ hour rollback buffer, and optimal infrastructure allocation.

title: Polaris v1 GA Launch - Final Go-Live Decision (Window C)

blocks.text: Polaris v1 GA Launch - Final Go-Live Decision
Decision Date: April 4, 2026
Decision Owner: Jorge Alvarez (Senior PM, Platform)
Executive Summary

After evaluating three candidate go-live windows against calendar commitments, SRE capacity constraints, and rollback buffer policy requirements, Window C (April 28-29, 2026) is confirmed as the only feasible launch window for Polaris v1 GA.
Constraint Analysis
Window A (April 14-15) - REJECTED
Hard conflict: Q2 Leadership Review (EVT-312) locked on April 15, 14:00-16:00
Mandatory exec meeting with VP Eng and CEO; cannot be rescheduled
Violates PM availability requirement during critical launch window
SRE capacity: 12 hours (adequate but not optimal)
Window B (April 21-22) - REJECTED
Rollback buffer: Only 48 hours before Auth Migration Checkpoint 2 (April 23)
VIOLATES mandatory 72-hour rollback buffer policy (Notion NPAG-9, section 3.2)
SRE capacity conflict: Split coverage between Polaris (Marcus) and auth (Sarah) creates resource contention
Risk: Polaris rollback extending into April 23-24 would block auth checkpoint
Window C (April 28-29) - CONFIRMED ✓
Calendar: Clean, no hard conflicts or locked leadership events
Rollback buffer: 96 hours before next platform milestone (May 2 monitoring review)
EXCEEDS mandatory 72-hour buffer by 24 hours
SRE capacity: 20 on-call hours, both primary (Marcus) and secondary (Rachel) coverage confirmed
Infrastructure: 95% compute allocation, 90% database pool, 95% CDN capacity
On-call rotation: Optimal team alignment per NPAG-9 schedule
Sign-Off
Confirmed by Jorge Alvarez (PM) on April 4, 2026 via Workmail (WMSG-5017)
Engineering Director (Priya Sharma) and SRE Lead (Marcus Chen) notified and acknowledged

Platform Team Decision Log - Week 14 (March 31 - April 4, 2026)
**Decision velocity this week: 4 decisions finalized, 2 deferred**
D-2026-031: Polaris Analytics Pipeline Capacity Allocation
**Decision**: Allocate 40% of data pipeline capacity to Polaris analytics workload starting April 7, with automatic scaling trigger at 75% utilization.

**Rationale**: Q2 OKR dependency requires real-time analytics for Polaris features. Current capacity modeling shows 40% allocation sufficient for projected load with 25% headroom. Automatic scaling prevents manual intervention during traffic spikes.
**Approved by**: Sarah Kim (VP Product), David Torres (Data Team Lead) - confirmed via Workmail thread WMSG-5009 on April 2
**Impact scope**: Data team, Platform team, affects Q2 analytics OKRs
D-2026-032: TechFlow Rate Limit Exception Policy
**Decision**: Grant TechFlow Industries temporary 3x rate limit increase (300 req/min → 900 req/min) for 45 days with mandatory usage review at day 30.

**Rationale**: Mid-market churn risk mitigation. TechFlow integration blocked by current limits. Temporary increase allows their Q2 rollout while we architect proper enterprise tier solution. 30-day checkpoint ensures we catch abuse patterns early.
**Approved by**: Jorge Alvarez (Platform PM), Rachel Kim (Customer Success VP) - finalized in meeting MTG-7004 on April 3
**Impact scope**: API infrastructure, customer success, sets precedent for rate limit exceptions
D-2026-033: Auth Migration Checkpoint Structure

**Decision**: Implement 3-checkpoint Go/No-Go structure for auth endpoint migration: (1) Internal services migration complete, (2) Customer notification sent + 14 days elapsed, (3) Legacy endpoint traffic < 5% for 48 hours.

**Rationale**: Reduces risk of customer-facing outages. Each checkpoint has clear success criteria and rollback procedure. 14-day customer notification window exceeds our standard 7-day policy but necessary given auth criticality.
**Approved by**: Priya Sharma (VP Engineering), Jorge Alvarez (Platform PM) - documented in Notion page NPAG-5, confirmed via Workmail WMSG-5006 on April 1
**Impact scope**: Engineering, customer success, affects migration timeline by +7 days
D-2026-034: Customer Notification Timeline for Auth Deprecation
**Decision**: Send customer notification on April 14, target legacy endpoint shutdown for May 5 (21-day notice period).

**Rationale**: Balances urgency of migration with customer communication best practices. 21 days exceeds contractual 14-day minimum, reduces churn risk for mid-market accounts already showing sensitivity.
**Approved by**: Rachel Kim (Customer Success VP), Jorge Alvarez (Platform PM) - finalized via TODO-507 completion and Workmail thread WMSG-5007
**Impact scope**: Customer success, engineering timeline, all API customers
Deferred Decisions

**DD-2026-008**: Q2 OKR final prioritization between data team and platform team proposals - deferred to April 8 leadership meeting. **Reason**: Requires VP Product and CTO alignment, both unavailable this week.

**DD-2026-009**: Polaris rollout communication strategy for Enterprise tier customers - deferred pending final GA date confirmation. **Reason**: Marketing team needs confirmed date before drafting messaging, GA date still has ±3 day variance.

title: Decision: Mid-Market Customer Retention Playbook Updates

blocks.text: Decision: Enhanced Mid-Market Retention Playbook
**Context**: Three mid-market accounts (TechFlow, DataSync, StartupHub) showed churn signals in past 6 weeks. Current playbook lacks escalation triggers for API integration blockers.

**Decision**: Update retention playbook to include: (1) Automatic escalation to Platform PM when customer reports API integration blocker, (2) 48-hour response SLA for rate limit or endpoint issues, (3) Weekly check-ins for accounts with active API escalations.

**Rationale**: API integration issues are leading indicator of churn for mid-market segment. Early escalation prevents frustration from building. 48-hour SLA balances urgency with engineering capacity.
**Approved by**: Rachel Kim (Customer Success VP), Jorge Alvarez (Platform PM)
**Implementation**: Customer Success team to begin using updated playbook April 7, 2026
